en: Naked, smeared with fragrant ashes,
holding a discus, trident, hand-drum, and mace,
seated in the lotus posture, and saluted by sages and gods.
Meditation on Dattātreya bestows the fulfillment of all desires. || 1 ||
In the lotus of the water at the *mūlādhāra*, which possesses four petals and is made vast by the very extensive syllables *vaṃ*, *śaṃ*, *ṣaṃ*, and *saṃ*,
one should contemplate the red-colored Lord Gaṇanātha.
I bow down to Dattātreya, the embodiment of the venerable Guru. || 2 ||
In the Svādhiṣṭhāna, within the six-petaled lotus at the subtle liṅga,
one should contemplate that yellow-colored Druhiṇa, who is the embodiment of Vākpati (Brahmā), with those letters ending in *ba* that are vast and exceedingly expansive.
I bow down to Dattātreya, the embodiment of the venerable Guru. || 3 ||
In the lotus at the navel, marked with ten petals and the syllables *ḍa* and *pha*, is the beloved of Lakṣmī, mounted upon Garuḍa, in the Maṇipūra center;
he is blue in color, of a quality-less form, and has the Vedas for his eyes.
I bow down to Dattātreya, the embodiment of the venerable Guru. || 4 ||
Within the heart-lotus, at its twelve petals, in the region of the letter *ka* at the end of the unstruck (*anāhata*) center, is the form of Śiva mounted upon a bull;
white-bodied, he performs the acts of creation, preservation, and dissolution.
I bow down to Dattātreya, the embodiment of the venerable Guru. || 5 ||
In the region of the throat, purified by the wheel, at the center of the lotus,
within a lunar orb of sixteen petals consisting of the vowels,
one should contemplate that Blessed One, the Lord of Māyā, the Jīva-Śiva.
I bow down to Dattātreya, the embodiment of the venerable Guru. || 6 ||
In the wheel of command (*ājñācakra*), at the location of the *bhṛkuṭī*, within the two petals,
is the seed-syllable *haṃ kṣaṃ*; he is the ocean of gnosis, the embodiment of the Guru,
the color of lightning, consisting of wisdom, and has an eye upon his forehead.
I bow down to Dattātreya, the embodiment of the venerable Guru. || 7 ||
In the lotus of water situated at the crown of the head, there is a white syllable, the seed of the moon;
upon its thousand petals known as "Lalanā," there are a thousand syllables called the seeds, ending with the fourth vowel.
I bow down to Dattātreya, the embodiment of the venerable Guru. || 8 ||
To Brahmānanda, to Mukunda, the Blessed One,
to that very Supreme Self who is the knowledge of Brahman, consisting of wisdom, the lordly sage of Brahman with his limbs smeared with ashes;
I bow down to Dattātreya, the embodiment of the venerable Guru. || 9 ||
